h: A year in the reeds at Barnes
p: One of the best things about the Wetland Centre is that it never looks the same twice. Come in spring and the sand martins are zipping back and forth over the water, with ducklings and goslings trailing after their parents along the edges of the pools. Summer belongs to the dragonflies and damselflies, which put on a proper show over the ponds on a warm afternoon, plus the wildflowers in the meadows. Autumn brings the first big flocks back to the main lake, and winter is the season the serious birders love, when the ducks build up in numbers and everyone has half an eye out for that bittern.

If you only do one thing, climb the Peacock Tower. It's a hide set over several floors on the far side of the main lake, and from the top you get a view across the whole reserve with the London skyline poking up behind it, which is a bit of a surreal combination. Families shouldn't miss the otters either, a firm favourite with younger visitors, and there are play spaces for when patience runs out.

Allow a good half-day to get round without rushing, longer if you're the type who sits in a hide waiting for a kingfisher. Bring binoculars if you have them, as they make a world of difference out on the lakes.

To build a bigger day, the Thames Path runs right past, so you can stroll the riverbank towards Putney or Hammersmith, and Kew Gardens is only a short hop west. Pack a flask and you've got a properly peaceful London day without the crowds.
